name: qdrant_health_check
description:
Confirm the configured Qdrant instance is reachable and responding.

Never raises to the caller: a health check that raises on the exact condition it exists to detect defeats its own purpose. Connection failures are logged and reported in the result's ok/error fields instead, so a client renders them without a tool-call error round-trip.

name: qdrant_collection_create
description:
Create a collection: either a single unnamed vector (`vector_size` + `distance`), or one or more named vectors (`vectors`, each a full `VectorParams` — size, distance, and optionally its own `multivector_config` for ColBERT-style multi-vectors or `quantization_config`) — exactly one of the two. `sparse_vectors` defines sparse (keyword-style) vectors at creation time. `quantization_config` (scalar/product/binary) and `strict_mode_config` apply to the whole collection.

`hnsw_config` and `optimizers_config` set the index and optimizer parameters from the start (they can also be changed later with `qdrant_collection_update`); `on_disk_payload=true` keeps payloads on disk instead of in RAM, which can only be chosen here.

Fails with a clear error if a collection with this name already exists.

Example (simple): {"collection_name": "docs", "vector_size": 4, "distance": "Cosine"} Example (hybrid): {"collection_name": "docs", "vectors": { "dense": {"size": 4, "distance": "Cosine"} }, "sparse_vectors": {"sparse": {}}} Example (multitenant index, payload on disk): {"collection_name": "docs", "vector_size": 4, "hnsw_config": {"m": 0, "payload_m": 16}, "on_disk_payload": true}

name: qdrant_collection_list
description:
List every collection name in the configured Qdrant instance.

Example: {}

name: qdrant_collection_info
qdrant_collection_update
qdrant_collection_delete
description:
Delete a collection and all its points; a no-op if it doesn't exist.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_collection_exists
description:
Check whether a collection exists, without raising if it doesn't.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_points_upsert
description:
Insert or replace points (id + vector + payload) in a collection.

`vector` matches the collection's vector config: a plain list for a single unnamed vector; a list of lists for an unnamed multivector; or a dict keyed by vector name for named vectors, where each value is a dense list, a multivector, or a sparse vector (`{"indices": [...], "values": [...]}`).

`update_mode` makes the write conditional: `insert_only` never overwrites an existing id, `update_only` never creates a new one (default `upsert` does both). `update_filter` only overwrites existing points whose current payload matches the filter. `wait=false` returns before the write is applied.

Fails with a clear error if the collection doesn't exist.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "points": [ {"id": 1, "vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "payload": {"city": "ny"}} ]} Example (named dense + sparse): {"collection_name": "docs", "points": [ {"id": 1, "vector": {"dense": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "sparse": {"indices": [1, 7], "values": [0.5, 0.2]}}} ]}

name: qdrant_points_get
qdrant_points_delete
qdrant_points_scroll
description:
Page through all points in a collection, optionally filtered.

Pass the returned `next_page_offset` as `offset` to fetch the next page; `null` means there are no more pages.

`order_by` sorts by a payload field instead of by id: a key, or `{"key": ..., "direction": "asc"|"desc", "start_from": value}`; the key needs a payload range index (integer, float or datetime). Paging works differently then: `offset` is rejected, and `next_page_offset` is always `null` even when more points remain — to continue, repeat the call with `start_from` set to the last value you received (points tied on that value are returned again, so de-duplicate by id).

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "limit": 50} Example (newest first): {"collection_name": "docs", "limit": 20, "order_by": {"key": "created_at", "direction": "desc"}}

name: qdrant_points_count
description:
Count points in a collection, optionally matching a filter.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_query
description:
Search a collection with Qdrant's unified Query API: vector similarity, hybrid fusion, multi-stage reranking, MMR diversity, payload-based score formulas, ordering by a payload field, or random sampling.

Exactly one query mode is required: - `query_vector` — nearest points to a dense vector, a multivector (list of vectors), a sparse vector (`{"indices": [...], "values": [...]}`), or a point id whose stored vector is reused. It must match the vector selected with `using`. Add `mmr` (`diversity` 0..1, `candidates_limit`) to re-order the nearest candidates for diversity: set `candidates_limit` well above `limit` (it defaults to `limit`, which leaves MMR nothing to choose from), and don't page an MMR query with `offset` — it is applied inside the `limit` re-ranked results (`offset` 1 with `limit` 2 returns one point); raise `limit` instead. - `fusion` + 2+ `prefetch` stages — combine retrieval strategies: `"rrf"` (Reciprocal Rank Fusion), `"dbsf"` (Distribution-Based Score Fusion), or `{"method": "rrf", "weights": [2, 1], "k": 60}` for RRF with one weight per stage (a count that doesn't match the stages is rejected by Qdrant). - `formula` — rescore the results of `prefetch` stages (required: a formula without prefetch is rejected). `{"expression": ..., "defaults": {...}}`. An expression is a number; a variable (`"$score"` is the prefetch score, any other string is a payload key); a payload condition (e.g. `{"key": "city", "match": {"value": "sf"}}`, worth 1 if it matches, else 0); or exactly one operator object: `{"sum": [...]}`, `{"mult": [...]}`, `{"neg": e}`, `{"abs": e}`, `{"div": {"left": e, "right": e}}`, `{"sqrt": e}`, `{"pow": {"base": e, "exponent": e}}`, `{"exp": e}`, `{"ln": e}`, `{"log10": e}`, `{"geo_distance": {"origin": {"lat": .., "lon": ..}, "to": "payload.key"}}`, `{"datetime": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`, `{"datetime_key": "payload.key"}`, and the decays `{"exp_decay" | "gauss_decay" | "lin_decay": {"x": e, "target": e, "scale": number, "midpoint": number}}`. A payload key a point lacks needs a value in `defaults`, or Qdrant rejects the query. - `order_by` — sort by a payload field instead of by similarity: a key or `{"key": ..., "direction": "asc"|"desc", "start_from": value}`. The key needs a payload range index (integer, float or datetime). - `sample: "random"` — random points.

A `prefetch` stage is itself a `query_vector` query or a `fusion` of its own nested `prefetch` stages, so pipelines nest: fuse dense+sparse in one stage, then rerank with a multivector. `using` selects a named vector; `lookup_from` resolves `query_vector` from a point id in another collection.

Tuning: `search_params` (`hnsw_ef`, `exact` for brute force, `quantization`: `ignore`/`rescore`/`oversampling`, `indexed_only`, `acorn`), `score_threshold` (drop weaker hits), `limit` + `offset` (paging), `timeout_seconds` (server-side), and `consistency` (a replica count, or `"majority"`/`"quorum"`/`"all"`; only meaningful on a replicated deployment). Fails with a clear error if the collection doesn't exist.

Example (plain): {"collection_name": "docs", "query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "limit": 5} Example (hybrid): {"collection_name": "docs", "fusion": "rrf", "prefetch": [ {"query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "using": "dense", "limit": 20}, {"query_vector": {"indices": [1, 7], "values": [0.5, 0.2]}, "using": "sparse", "limit": 20} ], "limit": 5} Example (diverse results): {"collection_name": "docs", "query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "mmr": {"diversity": 0.5, "candidates_limit": 50}, "limit": 5} Example (boost one city): {"collection_name": "docs", "prefetch": [ {"query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "limit": 50} ], "formula": {"expression": {"sum": ["$score", {"mult": [0.5, {"key": "city", "match": {"value": "sf"}}]}]}}, "limit": 5} Example (cheapest first): {"collection_name": "docs", "order_by": {"key": "price", "direction": "asc"}, "limit": 5}

name: qdrant_query_batch
description:
Run multiple independent queries against one collection in a single round trip — each item takes every query mode and tuning parameter of `qdrant_query` (plain vector, fusion over prefetch, MMR, formula, order_by, sample, search_params, score_threshold, offset); `timeout_seconds` and `consistency` apply to the whole batch.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "queries": [ {"query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "limit": 5}, {"query_vector": [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5], "limit": 5} ]}

name: qdrant_query_groups
description:
Vector query grouped by a payload field, up to `group_size` hits per group — e.g. the best-matching chunks per source document. Takes every query mode and tuning parameter of `qdrant_query` except `offset` (groups have no paging).

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "group_by": "document_id", "query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "group_size": 2}

name: qdrant_recommend
qdrant_recommend_batch
description:
Run multiple independent recommend queries against one collection in a single round trip. Each item takes the tuning parameters of `qdrant_recommend`; `timeout_seconds` and `consistency` apply to the whole batch.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "requests": [ {"positive": [1], "negative": [7]}, {"positive": [2, 3]} ]}

name: qdrant_recommend_groups
description:
Recommend query grouped by a payload field, up to `group_size` hits per group. Takes the tuning parameters of `qdrant_recommend` except `offset` (groups have no paging).

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "group_by": "document_id", "positive": [1, 2], "group_size": 2}

name: qdrant_discover
qdrant_discover_batch
description:
Run multiple independent discover queries against one collection in a single round trip. Each item takes the tuning parameters of `qdrant_discover`; `timeout_seconds` and `consistency` apply to the whole batch.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "requests": [ {"target": 1, "context": [{"positive": 2, "negative": 7}]} ]}

name: qdrant_distance_matrix_pairs
description:
Pairwise distance matrix between a random sample of points: for each of `sample` points, its `limit` closest neighbors among that same sample — returned as a flat list of (a, b, score) pairs.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "sample": 20, "limit": 5}

name: qdrant_distance_matrix_offsets
description:
Same distance matrix as `qdrant_distance_matrix_pairs`, in a column-oriented shape (offsets into a shared id list + a parallel score array) — more compact for large samples.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "sample": 20, "limit": 5}

name: qdrant_payload_set
description:
Merge fields into the payload of selected points — exactly one of `ids`/`points_filter`. Existing keys not in `payload` are kept. `key` sets a nested sub-field (e.g. `"metadata.author"`) instead of merging at the payload root.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "ids": [1], "payload": {"city": "ny"}}

name: qdrant_payload_overwrite
description:
Replace the entire payload of selected points with `payload` — exactly one of `ids`/`points_filter`. Unlike `qdrant_payload_set`, existing keys not in `payload` are dropped.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "ids": [1], "payload": {"city": "ny"}}

name: qdrant_payload_delete
description:
Delete specific payload keys from selected points — exactly one of `ids`/`points_filter`. Other keys are untouched.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "ids": [1], "keys": ["city"]}

name: qdrant_payload_clear
description:
Wipe the entire payload of selected points, keeping their vectors — exactly one of `ids`/`points_filter`.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "ids": [1]}

name: qdrant_payload_facet
description:
Count distinct values of a payload field across the collection (or a filtered subset) — e.g. how many points per `city`. `exact` trades speed for an exact count instead of an approximation.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "key": "city", "limit": 20}

name: qdrant_payload_index_create
description:
Create a payload index on `field_name`, speeding up filters that use it. `field_schema` can be a simple type name ("keyword", "integer", "float", "geo", "text", "bool", "datetime", "uuid") or a detailed params object (e.g. a `text` index with a specific tokenizer, or a `keyword` index marked `is_tenant`).

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "field_name": "city", "field_schema": "keyword"}

name: qdrant_payload_index_delete
description:
Delete the payload index on `field_name`.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "field_name": "city"}

name: qdrant_collection_vector_create
qdrant_collection_vector_delete
description:
Remove a named vector (dense or sparse) from a collection — points keep their other vectors and payload. Same server-version requirement as `qdrant_collection_vector_create`.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "vector_name": "sparse"}

name: qdrant_points_batch_update
description:
Run multiple point operations (upsert, delete, set/overwrite/delete/clear payload, update/delete vectors) atomically against one collection, in the order given. Each item is one of Qdrant's own tagged operation shapes, keyed by operation name.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "operations": [ {"upsert": {"points": [{"id": 1, "vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]}]}}, {"delete_payload": {"keys": ["city"], "points": [1]}} ]}

name: qdrant_vectors_update
description:
Replace the vector(s) of existing points by id — leaves their payload untouched. For a named-vector collection, `vector` is a dict keyed by vector name; for a single unnamed vector, pass a plain vector.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "points": [ {"id": 1, "vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]} ]}

name: qdrant_vectors_delete
description:
Remove specific named vectors from selected points, keeping their payload and other vectors — exactly one of `ids`/`points_filter`.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "vector_names": ["sparse"], "ids": [1]}

name: qdrant_alias_list
qdrant_collection_aliases
description:
List the aliases that point to one collection (an empty list if it has none). Fails with a clear error if the collection doesn't exist.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs_v2"}

name: qdrant_alias_update
description:
Create, rename, re-point or delete aliases — the basis of a zero-downtime reindex: build the new collection, then switch the alias that clients use.

Each operation is exactly one of `create_alias` (`collection_name`, `alias_name`), `rename_alias` (`old_alias_name`, `new_alias_name`) or `delete_alias` (`alias_name`). Operations run in order in one request but are NOT rolled back as a group: if a later one fails, the earlier ones stay applied (verified) — check `qdrant_alias_list` after an error. To switch an alias to another collection, send a single `create_alias`: on an alias name that already exists it re-points it, and a single operation is all-or-nothing.

Other verified behavior: deleting an alias that doesn't exist is a no-op, not an error; an alias can't take the name of an existing collection (409); creating one for a missing collection fails. Deleting a collection also removes the aliases that pointed to it. No collection data is ever modified.

Example (zero-downtime switch): {"operations": [ {"create_alias": {"collection_name": "docs_v2", "alias_name": "docs"}} ]} Example (rename then delete): {"operations": [ {"rename_alias": {"old_alias_name": "docs", "new_alias_name": "docs_old"}}, {"delete_alias": {"alias_name": "docs_old"}} ]}

name: qdrant_collection_cluster_info
description:
Shard layout of a collection: how many shards it has and, for each local shard, its point count and replica state. Works on a single-node deployment too (one peer, `remote_shards` empty); shard transfers and resharding only ever appear on a distributed deployment. Fails with a clear error if the collection doesn't exist.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_collection_optimizations
qdrant_collection_copy
description:
Copy points (all vectors — dense, sparse and multivector — and payload) from one collection to another of the same Qdrant instance, entirely server-side: the vectors never pass through the model.

The target must already exist with a compatible vector configuration (see `qdrant_collection_info`); this tool does not create it. Use it to re-create a collection with another distance, quantization or HNSW layout, then switch an alias with `qdrant_alias_update`.

Each call copies at most `max_points` points, in batches of `batch_size`, so no single call runs long. If the result has `done: false`, call again with the same arguments and `offset=next_offset`. Points that already exist in the target under the same id are overwritten, so re-running a copy is safe; points that were deleted from the source are not removed from the target. `copy_filter` copies only matching points. Points are visited in id order, so points added to the source with a lower id than the current offset during a long copy are not picked up.

If a batch fails, the error reports how many points were copied and the `offset` to resume from.

Example: {"source_collection": "docs_v1", "target_collection": "docs_v2"} Example (continue): {"source_collection": "docs_v1", "target_collection": "docs_v2", "offset": 1000}

name: qdrant_payload_schema_infer
description:
Profile the payload keys that actually occur in a collection, so filters can be written against real keys instead of guessed ones.

Looks at a random sample of `sample_size` points (optionally limited by `sample_filter`) and reports, per key: the value types seen (`string`, `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `null`), whether it was ever an array, how many sampled points have it (`present_in`), and whether it has a payload index (`indexed`, `index_type`). Keys use the syntax filters expect: `a.b` for nested objects, `a[].b` for objects inside an array. For keys with a keyword/integer/uuid/bool index, `top_values` adds the most frequent values over the **whole collection** (not just the sample), taken from the index; set it to 0 to skip. Also lists indexed keys that no sampled point has (`indexed_but_unseen`).

Because it is a sample, a rare key can be missed: raise `sample_size` (up to 1000) if a field you expect doesn't show up. At most `max_fields` keys are returned, most common first (`fields_truncated` says if more existed).

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_snapshot_create
description:
Create a snapshot of one collection's current state.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_snapshot_list
description:
List the snapshots stored for one collection.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_snapshot_delete
description:
Delete a collection snapshot, freeing its disk space on the server — does not touch the live collection.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "snapshot_name": "docs-....snapshot"}

name: qdrant_snapshot_recover
qdrant_snapshot_download
description:
Confirm a collection snapshot exists and return where to fetch it from — this tool does not transfer the (potentially huge) snapshot file itself; download it yourself (e.g. `curl`) from the returned `url`.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "snapshot_name": "docs-....snapshot"}

Create a snapshot of the whole storage (every collection and server config), not just one collection.

Example: {}

name: qdrant_storage_snapshot_list
description:
List the full-storage snapshots stored on the server.

Example: {}

description:
Delete a full-storage snapshot, freeing its disk space.

Example: {"snapshot_name": "full-....snapshot"}

qdrant_telemetry
description:
Server-wide telemetry: build info, per-collection stats, request counters, memory and hardware usage. Not tied to any one collection.

Return the URL where Qdrant serves Prometheus-format metrics — this tool does not fetch the metrics themselves (they're plain text, not JSON); point your Prometheus scraper at the returned `url` instead.

description:
Current server-wide resource quotas (memory/disk limits) and actual usage.

Example: {}

Update server-wide resource quotas. Only the fields you pass are changed; omitted ones keep their current value.

Example: {"enabled": true, "max_resident_memory_percent": 90}

name: qdrant_issues_list
description:
List the issues Qdrant has detected about its own configuration (e.g. a heavily-filtered field with no payload index). **API Beta** in Qdrant itself — the exact shape can change without notice, so this is returned as-is rather than forced into a fixed schema.

Example: {}

name: qdrant_issues_clear
description:
Clear all accumulated issues.

Example: {}
